title: Older People and Palliative Care
full_title: Medicine for Older People and Palliative Care
tagline: Ageing and frailty, falls, delirium, polypharmacy, symptom control and care at the end of life
summary: An ageing population makes the care of older people central to medicine. This course covers ageing and frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment, falls, delirium and dementia care, polypharmacy and deprescribing, and palliative care: symptom control, communication and care at the end of life.
overview: Older patients are not simply young patients with more diseases. Physiological reserve narrows, so illness often presents as confusion, a fall or loss of function rather than with the textbook signs; several conditions and many medicines interact; and a hospital admission can itself cause harm. Geriatric medicine is the specialty of the problem with many causes, and its methods are comprehensive geriatric assessment, an interdisciplinary team, and plans built around what matters to the person. This course teaches the core of the specialty: ageing and frailty, falls, delirium and dementia care, and polypharmacy.

Palliative medicine is the other half of the same skill: relieving suffering when cure is not possible, from early in a serious illness and not only in the last days. Chapters cover the principles of palliative care, illness trajectories and advance care planning; the control of pain, breathlessness, nausea, constipation and other symptoms; and care in the last days of life, after death and in bereavement, with the UK legal framework for end-of-life decisions.

The approach is practical and, where possible, quantitative: the Clinical Frailty Scale and frailty index, the Cockcroft–Gault equation for drug dosing, lying and standing blood pressure, the 4AT and its predictive value, numbers needed to treat, anticholinergic burden, and the arithmetic of opioid doses and conversions. All cases are fictional, and statements about management describe principles under current UK guidance (mainly NICE), with doses always taken from a current formulary and local guidelines.
outcomes: Explain how ageing reduces physiological reserve and why this leads to atypical presentations, geriatric syndromes and altered drug handling.
Define frailty, grade it with the Clinical Frailty Scale and a frailty index, and describe appropriate and inappropriate uses of frailty scores.
Describe comprehensive geriatric assessment, its domains and team, and the evidence that it improves outcomes for frail older inpatients.
Assess an older person who has fallen, distinguishing mechanical, syncopal and multifactorial falls, and outline evidence-based multifactorial prevention.
Recognise delirium with a screening tool, identify its precipitants, and describe its prevention and management, including the cautious use of antipsychotics.
Outline the care of people with dementia in general settings, including distressed behaviour, and apply the Mental Capacity Act framework for decisions.
Identify problematic polypharmacy and prescribing cascades, use explicit criteria such as STOPP/START, and plan safe deprescribing.
Define palliative care, recognise people who may be in the last year of life, and describe communication and advance care planning.
Manage common symptoms in advanced illness, including the calculation of opioid total daily doses, breakthrough doses and conversions.
Recognise dying, plan care in the last days of life, verify and certify death, and support bereaved people within the UK legal framework.

history.title: A disease of the cortex described
history.detail: Alois Alzheimer presents the case of Auguste Deter, a woman in her fifties with progressive memory loss and behavioural change whose brain showed the plaques and tangles now associated with Alzheimer's disease. Emil Kraepelin names the disease after him in 1910.

history.title: Geriatrics named
history.detail: The New York physician Ignatz Nascher coins the word 'geriatrics' and argues that the diseases of old age deserve their own branch of medicine.

history.title: Assessment and rehabilitation on the chronic wards
history.detail: Marjory Warren takes charge of the chronic wards at the West Middlesex Hospital, assesses and rehabilitates patients assumed to need lifelong care, and discharges many of them home. Her methods are the origin of comprehensive geriatric assessment and of geriatric medicine as a specialty in Britain.

history.title: Measuring daily function
history.detail: Sidney Katz and colleagues publish the index of activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, continence and feeding), giving clinicians and researchers a standard way to record function in older people.

history.title: St Christopher's Hospice opens
history.detail: Cicely Saunders, who trained as a nurse, a medical social worker and a doctor, opens St Christopher's Hospice in Sydenham, London, combining care of the dying with teaching and research and introducing the concept of total pain.

history.title: Palliative care named
history.detail: The Canadian surgeon Balfour Mount opens a palliative care service at the Royal Victoria Hospital in Montreal, coining the term 'palliative care' for hospice-style care within a teaching hospital.

history.title: Falls are predictable
history.detail: Mary Tinetti and colleagues show in a cohort of people aged 75 and over that the risk of falling rises steeply with the number of risk factors, from 8% with none to 78% with four or more, turning falls from accidents into a preventable syndrome.

history.title: Delirium made measurable
history.detail: Sharon Inouye and colleagues publish the Confusion Assessment Method; in 1999 her team's trial of the Hospital Elder Life Program shows that delirium in hospital can be prevented.

history.title: Frailty defined and measured
history.detail: Linda Fried and colleagues define the frailty phenotype using the Cardiovascular Health Study, and Kenneth Rockwood and Arnold Mitnitski describe frailty as the accumulation of deficits; both predict falls, disability and death.

references.title: Oxford Textbook of Geriatric Medicine (3rd edition)
references.authors: Jean-Pierre Michel, B. Lynn Beattie, Finbarr C. Martin, Jeremy D. Walston (eds)
references.note: A comprehensive international reference on the medicine of older people, from the biology of ageing to services.

references.title: Brocklehurst's Textbook of Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology (8th edition)
references.authors: Howard M. Fillit, Kenneth Rockwood, John Young (eds)
references.note: A long-established textbook with strong chapters on frailty, falls and comprehensive geriatric assessment.

references.title: Oxford Textbook of Palliative Medicine (6th edition)
references.authors: Nathan Cherny, Marie Fallon, Stein Kaasa, Russell K. Portenoy, David C. Currow (eds)
references.note: The standard reference for specialist palliative medicine, including symptom control and communication.

references.title: Palliative Care Formulary (PCF9, 9th edition)
references.authors: Andrew Wilcock, Paul Howard, Clare Stark Toller, Joanne Droney, Sarah Charlesworth (eds)
references.note: The UK reference for drugs used in palliative care, including opioid conversion tables and syringe pump compatibility.

references.title: Falls: assessment and prevention in older people and in people 50 and over at higher risk (NG249)
references.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
references.note: Current NICE guideline on identifying people at risk of falls, multifactorial assessment and interventions; replaced CG161.

references.title: Delirium: prevention, diagnosis and management in hospital and long-term care (CG103)
references.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
references.note: NICE guidance on delirium risk reduction, recognition and treatment (first published 2010, last updated 2023).

references.title: Care of dying adults in the last days of life (NG31)
references.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
references.note: NICE guidance on recognising dying, communication, hydration and anticipatory prescribing.

references.title: STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3
references.authors: Denis O'Mahony, Antonio Cherubini, Anna Renom Guiteras et al.
references.note: European Geriatric Medicine 14:625-632; the 133 STOPP and 57 START criteria used in structured medication review.
